headline: Over 1,100 exotic animals seized in Dhaka, police hunt masterminds
summary: Police have recovered a massive haul of illegal wildlife, sparking a crackdown on the illicit trade of exotic species in the capital.
details: Police in Dhaka have seized over 1,100 exotic animals in a major operation targeting the illegal wildlife trade. The haul includes various species of rare and non-native animals.

Authorities are now actively hunting for the masterminds behind this large-scale smuggling operation. The seizure represents a significant blow to the illicit trade networks operating within the city.
The illegal trade of exotic animals often involves poor living conditions for the animals and violates national and international wildlife protection laws.
Police are continuing their investigations to uncover the full extent of the network and arrest those responsible for the मुद्दे (issue) issue of illegal animal trafficking.

headline_marked: Jubo Dal [[expels 300 leaders and activists]] nationwide
headline: Jubo Dal expels 300 leaders and activists nationwide
summary: President Abdul Monayem Munna stated that those removed were involved in activities contrary to the organisation's ideals.
details: Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal has expelled around 300 leaders and activists across the country. The decision follows allegations of activities that were deemed contrary to the organization's ideals.

President Abdul Monayem Munna announced the move during a press conference at a hotel in Nayapaltan, Dhaka. He stated that criminal cases have also been filed against many of the expelled members to protect the organization's reputation.

Munna emphasized that no person or group would be allowed to carry out illegal activities while using the organization's name. He added that some disciplinary actions were withdrawn after further investigation.

The organization's disciplinary process involves union-level cases being handled by district committees, while central body handles offenses involving upazila or district-level leaders. Law enforcement and intelligence agencies are also engaged in the investigations.
